subject: Quantum Retail — onboarding runbook & bench plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Puri <samir@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Quantum Retail — onboarding runbook & bench plan

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, attached is the lightweight runbook and the proposed load plan we'll use for acceptance benchmarking. High-level goals we agreed to:

- Throughput target: 350 concurrent inference sessions (p95 throughput target of 280 requests/sec across the cluster)
- Latency targets: 95th percentile tail <= 220ms for 512-token requests, median ~45ms as the operational guide
- Test window: 3 days of controlled load plus 24-hour overnight soak with production-sim traffic

What I'd like to confirm from you: the preferred time to run the controlled load (we suggested Tue/Wed next week), whether you want any additional payload variance (longer chat context vs short prompts), and if Ops will permit the VPC egress for telemetry to our console during tests.

Attachments: quantum_onboard_loadplan.csv (load ramp & payload matrix), runbook_v1.md (step-by-step acceptance checklist).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm Tue 11/10 09:00 ET start OR suggest a different window.
2) Ben to finalize pricing addendum for the dedicated burst window we discussed.
3) Monica to own test execution and results bundle.

If that sounds good I'll lock the calendar invites and create the results folder on Drive.

Thanks —
Logan
Logan Wright | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199
From: Samir Puri <samir@quantumretail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: techops@quantumretail.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Quantum Retail — onboarding runbook & bench plan

Logan —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications before we lock things:

- The 350 concurrent sessions looks reasonable; can we cap bursts at 420 for a 10-minute stress window to validate autoscaling behavior?
- For latency targets, could you add a small sample of 1024-token prompts? We need to understand tail behavior for long-context retrieval use cases.
- Ops confirmed the VPC egress but requests that telemetry be limited to the test window and sampling rate 1:10 to reduce telemetry volume.

We'll tentatively confirm Tue 11/10 09:00 ET. I'll loop in Alex from Ops (cc'd on the next mail) to confirm firewall rules if anything changes.

—Samir
Samir Puri | Head of ML Ops, Quantum Retail
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Puri <samir@quantumretail.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Quantum Retail — onboarding runbook & bench plan

Ben / Monica — forwarding Samir's confirmation. Key updates to incorporate:

- Add a 10-minute burst phase capped at 420 concurrent sessions (we'll observe autoscaler transitions and GPU fill rates).
- Include a small batch of 1024-token payloads (5% of requests during the soak).
- Telemetry sampling 1:10 and the telemetry window must be limited to the scheduled test window.

Monica: can you update runbook_v1.md and quantum_onboard_loadplan.csv to reflect the burst phase and long-context sample? Please also add a short section that lists the exact console traces we'll share (per-route p50/p95/p99, GPU util, KV cache hit rate, error counts).

Ben: Samir mentioned pricing for a dedicated burst window — can you prepare the two-line addendum for dedicated capacity + one-time test credit so Procurement has the right docs when they sign? I want that in place before the test so there are no billing surprises.

I'll send the calendar invite once Monica confirms the updated artifacts.

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Samir Puri <samir@quantumretail.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Quantum Retail — onboarding runbook & bench plan (results folder & pre-test checklist)

Samir —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming the window. Per the changes we made: attached is the updated load plan (quantum_onboard_loadplan.csv) and the preliminary results template (latency_results_summary.pdf) which we'll populate during the run. I also updated runbook_v1.md to call out the burst window and the 5% 1024-token payload mix.

Pre-test checklist (day-of):
- Redwood: provision dedicated burst capacity and enable the autoscaler debug trace for the run.
- Quantum Ops: confirm short-term firewall rule for telemetry (we will only send sampled traces 1:10).
- Test harness: ensure seed keys for deterministic prompts are set and dataset shuffle disabled for the controlled run.
- Observability: monitor p50/p95/p99 per-route, GPU util, KV cache hit-rate; immediate rollback criteria = sustained p95 > 450ms or error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes.

Deliverables we'll share within 6 business hours of test completion:
1) Latency + throughput time series + snapshots (pdf + csv)
2) Console trace export + raw telemetry (sampled)
3) Short findings note with risk items and suggested config changes (if any)

If all good I'll produce the calendar invite for Tue 11/10 09:00 ET (60m controlled window + 24h soak).

Attachments: quantum_onboard_loadplan.csv, latency_results_summary.pdf, runbook_v1.md

Best,
Monica Patel | Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
